stem: A tissue-culture line remains visually uniform through several passages. What conclusion about genetic fidelity is strongest?
choices: Visual uniformity proves complete genetic identity
Visual consistency is useful but does not prove absence of somaclonal or molecular variation; fidelity should be evaluated with appropriate records and tests for the use case
No further identity control is ever needed
rationale: Phenotypic appearance cannot fully establish genetic identity. Germplasm quality systems should preserve provenance and use appropriate fidelity checks for the intended risk level.
